properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL (Anthony, 2026-10-12, thinking out loud, continuing dec:idea-what-is-the-one-story-of-what-reflow2-is-and-is-not; nothing here is chosen).

His words: "the explanation of reflow2 should almost be decomposed down to "the human decision process". The human decision process is a multi-step cognitive sequence where the brain gathers information, evaluates alternatives, and selects a course of action influenced by logic, emotions, values, and mental shortcuts."

The model he gave:
- Key stages: Problem Recognition (realizing a choice or change is needed); Information Search (internal data such as memories and feelings, and external data such as facts and advice); Evaluating Alternatives (against personal goals and values); Making the Choice (committing to one option); Outcome Evaluation & Learning (assessing whether the result was satisfying, to guide future choices).
- The two systems of thought: System 1, fast and intuitive (automatic, emotional, unconscious; daily routines); System 2, slow and deliberate (logical, analytical, conscious; complex problems).
- Influences and biases: cognitive biases (confirmation bias, anchoring); emotions (fear, excitement, loss aversion); brain mechanics (the drift-diffusion model: evidence accumulates until it crosses a threshold that triggers an action; The Decision Lab).

His conclusion: "I feel like for the most part, reflow2 is about this".

HOW THE STAGES COULD MAP ONTO WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY DOES. These are candidates to react to, not chosen wording:
1. Problem recognition: gaps and open questions say what is undecided or missing, and a change shows what it touches.
2. Information search: the design is the project's memory, both internal (what was decided, measured and tried before) and external (findings, documents, other designs). The AI searches it before proposing anything.
3. Evaluating alternatives: ideas are recorded as ideas, with their counter-arguments beside them, and roads not taken are kept.
4. Making the choice: only the person settles intent (rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word), dated and with the reason.
5. Outcome evaluation and learning: verifications, findings marked measured or forecast, root cause before a fix, and accepted decisions the bad news reaches (choices_in_doubt).

WAYS TO USE IT, none chosen:
(a) Use the five stages as the spine of the explainer pages: one stage, what goes wrong for people and for AI at that stage, and what reflow2 does about it.
(b) Use the biases as the "why": confirmation bias, anchoring, and the AI's overconfidence, each beside the check that answers it (docs/partnership.md already maps the AI's half).
(c) Use System 1 and System 2 as an analogy: the AI answers fluently and fast, like System 1, and reflow2's checks make room for System 2 (a measurement that could prove the favourite wrong, a reason written down) at the moments that matter.
(d) Use only the five plain-word stages on the first page, and keep the psychology for a deeper page.

ADDED THE SAME DAY, his words: "I think this is why reflow2 can be used for so many things because most of it comes down that whether it is designing a complex process or planning a wrestling season (like my brother is using it for) - they all kind of boil down to the human decision process". So the decision process is offered as the REASON reflow2 generalises. req:design-anything (accepted) already says reflow2 is for any project; this says why: every project, technical or not, is a run of decisions.

Counter, recorded beside it: dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-project-that-is-not-software is still open and says the DELIVERY is software-shaped (requirements, capabilities, components, artifacts, drift against code), even though the vocabulary is neutral. A coach planning a season meets that toolchain. So the decision process may be the part that generalises, and the code-coherence layer the part that does not, or not yet. A story that promises "any decision" should say which half a non-software user gets.

The brother's season is one case. How well it works for him is not measured here, and a page should not use his real design or name him without his say. A made-up sports example in the Gearheads' style fits the settled rule that hand-written pages use made-up examples (dec:the-sites-setup-pages-are-hand-written-and-its-design-pages-stay-generated).
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-12 — promoted into: the site's story follows the human decision process in everyday words, with the psychology on a deeper page as a likeness
properties.rationale:
Counter-arguments and costs, recorded beside the idea, not against it:

1. IT FITS THE "WHY" HALF BETTER THAN THE "WHAT WAS BUILT" HALF. reflow2 also keeps design and code in agreement: drift caught, verification, releases, what ships. The decision lens covers much of that as outcome evaluation, but a reader could come away thinking reflow2 is a decision journal and miss that it follows the work into the code. The vision's "concept to operations" is wider than one decision.

2. DO NOT OVERCLAIM ON BIAS. reflow2 cannot remove a person's bias. It can put the evidence, the alternatives and the counter-argument in front of them, and record what was measured against what was assumed. The AI has biases of its own: it agrees with the person, which amplifies confirmation bias, and it states guesses with confidence. That actually strengthens the partnership story, because the graph's recorded counter-arguments and refutable measurements push back where both people and AI lean. But "reflow2 prevents bias" would be false.

3. THE PSYCHOLOGY IS AN ANALOGY, NOT A MECHANISM. System 1 and 2 and drift-diffusion are frameworks about brains. Mapping an AI or a graph onto them is a metaphor. Said as "like", it helps; said as "is", it invites a scientist (NSLS-II) to stop reading. Drift-diffusion is the weakest fit for a non-technical page.

4. THE PLAIN-WORDS GOAL. His earlier point is that non-technical readers should not be intimidated. The five stages are everyday words (notice, look into it, weigh options, decide, learn), so they suit the first page. The terms System 1/2, anchoring and drift-diffusion suit a second page. That fits the 2-3 page split in dec:idea-what-is-the-one-story-of-what-reflow2-is-and-is-not.

5. COST: (a), (b) and (d) are words on the explainer pages, and (b) reuses docs/partnership.md. (c) is a paragraph. None needs code.

6. SETTLED GROUND THIS STANDS ON: dec:three-party-checks (the LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides) and rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word (the choice is the person's). Both already say stage 4 belongs to the human.
